findings: Native BF16 codec uses 64-row global tiles and four 16-row warp groups; offsets and kernel lookup strides explicitly encode four warp groups.
Changing only BLOCK_ROW_WARPS from four to two would break codec addressing.
Only the full 64-row tile is padded: common bytes to multiples of 16, rare BF16 counts to multiples of eight. Mid-tile warp offsets are not guaranteed aligned.
A 32-row candidate would require parent-tile indexing, half-tile metadata and aligned staging windows with adjusted local decoder offsets.
Full K accumulation could remain in original order, but byte and arithmetic equality require GPU qualification.
Reducing rows per block preserves total useful warp work; doubled block count alone does not establish higher achieved occupancy or speed.
The previous compact/narrow/tail-first failures remain relevant; do not repeat unchanged candidates.
decision: Do not change the running kernel. If C16 fails the speed target, profile a new mechanism before integration; a half-row layout requires a CPU codec/addressing oracle before GPU execution.
limits: The inspected L_API.cu is the retained diagnostic control build with an appended resource-query ABI, not a new claim about the qualified production library hash.
This is source analysis, not a measured 32-row candidate or a performance prediction.
